Where should we start with AI?
With one repetitive, high-volume job that already has clear rules, such as answering order questions or processing invoices. It is quick to measure, and it builds trust before you automate more.
Yes. We mask personal data before it reaches a model, use providers that do not train on your data, apply role-based access and keep an audit log. We can also run models inside your own cloud.
What if the AI gets something wrong?
We design for it. Important actions need approval, low-confidence answers go to a person, and we track accuracy after launch so problems show up early.
Will it work with our current systems?
Almost always. We connect through APIs, webhooks, databases or, when there is nothing else, the screens your team already uses.

How is an agent different from a chatbot?
A chatbot answers. An agent acts: it plans several steps, uses your tools and completes a task, usually with an approval step before anything important.
Can an agent spend money or delete things by mistake?
Only if you let it. We set explicit permissions, spending caps and approval gates, and sensitive actions always ask first.
Which tools can it connect to?
Anything with an API, plus email, calendars, databases, spreadsheets and, when needed, web portals through a controlled browser.
How do we know it is working?
We give you a dashboard of completed tasks, errors, cost and time saved, along with a log of every run.
